Investigation at main `903e420b3a6443330233d3e58386d84100a21c5e`:

- The unchanged exact test passes on Linux: one passed, 28 filtered out, 1.05 s.
- The complete `mcp_live` binary passes on Linux: 29 passed, no failures or ignored tests, 6.72 s.
- `Inbox::listen_with_idle` uses loopback TCP on Windows and Linux. This test does not use a named pipe or the UI link.
- The native clock is `std::time::Instant` on both systems.
- The listener retries `WouldBlock`, `TimedOut` and `Interrupted`. The Rust-documented timeout error difference is already handled.
- Microsoft documents an indeterminate connection state after a blocking receive timeout with `SO_RCVTIMEO`. The listener performs repeated timed reads before its best-effort idle write. This is a relevant transport constraint, not proof of this failure's cause.

Source: [Microsoft SOL_SOCKET options, SO_RCVTIMEO](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/sol-socket-socket-options).

The missing evidence is the Windows panic location and message, including the native error if a read failed. A six-second summary does not identify whether notification, lower bound or close failed. No Windows target or runtime is installed here. I did not access a runner or change host setup.

Please capture the unchanged test on an existing Windows checkout at this revision, or another revision with the same test and listener. In PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:RUST_BACKTRACE = "1"
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live -- idle_timeout::a_configured_finite_window_expires_on_the_listener --exact --nocapture 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath issue-4252-windows.log
rustc -Vv
```

Include the tested commit and full log. If it passes alone but fails in the binary, capture the full `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live -- --nocapture` output instead.

No source or assertion changed. No commit, push or PR was made. I will not infer Windows success from Linux results or replace the socket test with a policy-only test that does not verify notification and close.
